Open a break-glass window on a repository-managed policy: for `durationHours` (1 to 168, default 24) an administrator may change it from the dashboard. A reason is required and a passkey confirmation for action `policy_break_glass`. Every change made meanwhile is a break-glass release that leaves the live policy ahead of the repository; nothing is undone when the window ends. Every administrator is notified. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

get.summary: The live policy as files that compile back to it: `policy.yaml` for the sections and one enveloped file per kind in the document ("download as code"). `contentHash` identifies what was exported, and `releaseId` is the live release it came from. Packs a document extended are folded into its sections. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

post.summary: Switch off everything above a read for agents (`scope` `tools`) and every call between agents (`scope` `a2a`, which also stops every running chain), in one signed release; both by default. It can only tighten. An administrator needs a passkey confirmation for action `policy_freeze`; a repository's CI job (a SIEM or SOAR pipeline) calls it with a policy token that carries `policy:freeze`, which only a job on the policy branch that no pull request started is given. While a repository manages the policy the release is a break-glass one.

put.summary: Hand the policy to its repository (`git`) or back to the dashboard. Both need a passkey confirmation for action `policy_management_change` (`401 step_up_required` names the digest; confirm, then send the same request again). Switching to `git` needs a connected repository (`409 policy_repo_missing`) and a last apply from the repository that equals the live policy (`409 policy_git_apply_differs`), so the switch changes nothing. While `git` manages the policy, dashboard and pack writes answer `409 policy_managed_in_git`. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

post.summary: Author a private policy pack version and publish it to the organization's catalog. The document is checked as a policy that extends it would check it, so a pack no document could use never publishes; it holds no `org`, `security`, `cedar` or credential. A version is immutable: the same name and version with different content answers `409`, with the same content `200`. A pack is usable by `extends` once the catalog has published it. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

get.summary: A repository's apply that is held for approval: its status (`pending`, `applied`, `denied`, `expired` or `superseded`) and, for a signed-in administrator, the plan to review. A CI job with `policy:apply` reads the status to wait for the decision.

post.summary: Approve or deny a held apply. Both need a passkey confirmation for action `policy_apply_approve`, made for this apply, its content and the decision (`401 step_up_required` names the digest; confirm, then send the same request again). Approving applies the candidate exactly as it was held; an apply the policy has moved past answers `409 policy_conflict` and is stale for good, one already decided `409 policy_pending_decided`, one nobody approved in time `410 policy_pending_expired`. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

Judge policy files against the live policy (or the release `base` names) without applying them: the changes with file and line, whether they loosen protection, the identities each change reaches, the credentials a person of each group could still register, and the decisions that move for particular call arguments. `detail: summary` leaves out values and member emails, for places members are not meant to be named. The plan is kept for 30 days and returned with a Markdown rendering. Owners and admins in a browser session, or a repository's CI job with a policy token that carries `policy:plan`.

get.summary: A kept plan, in full. Plans are kept for 30 days; after that this answers `404`. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

The organization's policy releases, newest first. Each names who made it, when, and whether it is the live one; the policy values a release holds are never returned. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

post.summary: Apply a policy document as one signed release: every section, and every enveloped document, is written in one transaction or none is. The files are compiled first; the change is judged against what is live now, never against the last release. A change that loosens protection needs a passkey confirmation made for exactly this release (`401 step_up_required` names the action and digest to confirm; confirm, then send the same request again). `expectedParentId` is the release the caller planned against: another live release, or a policy write that landed while the apply was running, answers `409 policy_conflict`. Owners and admins in a browser session. A repository's CI job applies with a policy token that carries `policy:apply`, which only a job on the policy branch that no pull request started is given; the release is then a repository release, its commit and repository taken from the token. Before anything is written the provider is asked whether the commit is signed and how many people approved the pull request that merged it, when the repository requires either (`403 policy_commit_unverified`, `403 policy_approvals_missing`; a provider that cannot be asked is `503 policy_verification_unavailable`, never a pass). A repository's change that loosens protection is held for an administrator's passkey approval unless the organization chose otherwise (strict mode always holds it): the answer is `202` with the held apply, which expires after 72 hours.

get.summary: One release: who made it, why, which top-level sections differ from the release before it, and any upstreams a rollback left out. The policy values are never returned. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

post.summary: Make an earlier release's policy live again, as a new signed release; history only grows. The change is judged against what is live now. A rollback that loosens protection needs a passkey confirmation for action `policy_rollback`, made for exactly this release (`401 step_up_required` names the action and digest; confirm, then send the same request again). An upstream the earlier release names that has been deleted since is left out and listed in `skippedUpstreams`. `expectedParentId` is the release the caller saw as live: another live release, or a policy write that landed meanwhile, answers `409 policy_conflict`. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

delete.summary: Disconnect the repository. Needs a passkey confirmation for action `policy_repo_change`, and the policy must be handed back to the dashboard first (`409 policy_managed_in_git`). Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

get.summary: The repository the organization's policy is connected to, with its settings, or `null`. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

put.summary: Connect the policy to its repository, or change its settings. Needs a passkey confirmation for action `policy_repo_change` (`401 step_up_required` names the digest; confirm, then send the same request again). A GitHub repository is trusted through the App installation the organization linked, and the repository's workflows may then trade their identity token at `/api/policy/ci/token`. A GitLab project must first prove it owns the project: until it has, the answer is `202` with the challenge its pipeline answers with an identity token (the same trust screen as evaluations verifies it), and the request is sent again. A GitLab connection answers the project's webhook token once. While a repository manages the policy it cannot be swapped for another (`409 policy_managed_in_git`). Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

delete.summary: Forget the stored GitLab project access token. An apply from a project that requires signed commits or approvals is then refused until a token is stored again. Needs a passkey confirmation for action `policy_repo_change`. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

put.summary: Store the project access token of the GitLab policy project. It is tried against the project first, then sealed with the organization's key; it is never returned. With it Zuano checks signed commits and merge request approvals before an apply, follows the branch head, comments on merge requests and opens merge requests. Needs a passkey confirmation for action `policy_repo_change` (`401 step_up_required` names the digest; confirm, then send the same request again). Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

get.summary: Who manages the policy now (the dashboard or its repository), the live release, the repository, an open break-glass window, the drift between the two and the applies waiting for approval. Browser sessions only; owners and admins.

post.summary: Compile policy files for this organization and report what they contain, or every problem found (`422 policy_invalid`, each with file, line and path). Nothing is written and the live policy is not read. Owners and admins in a browser session, or a repository's CI job with a policy token that carries `policy:plan`.
The redacted session a request would produce, with what was replaced. Nothing is stored. Rate limited.

get.summary: List the organization’s projects.

post.summary: Create a project.

delete.summary: Delete a project and revoke its keys.

get.summary: Read a project. A server key may read its own project only.

patch.summary: Change a project’s settings, or suspend and resume it.

post.summary: Make a new secret for verifying the signed parameters a connect link adds to the callback address. It is shown once; the old one stops working at once.

get.summary: List a project’s keys. Secrets are never returned.

post.summary: Create a server key. The token is shown once.

delete.summary: Revoke a key.

get.summary: Recipes proposed from the organization’s own recorded tool calls, newest evidence first. A candidate holds tool names and their order only and is never served until an admin accepts it and the draft it becomes is activated.

post.summary: Turn a candidate into a draft recipe. Send `recipe` to save your own wording instead; then a different admin has to activate it.
Dismiss a candidate; mining the same pattern again does not bring it back.

get.summary: List the organization’s recipes and the platform’s active ones, except a platform recipe the organization has overridden.

post.summary: Write an organization recipe as a draft. Every tool must exist, steps must hold together, and the text may hold no addresses, identifiers, long numbers or secrets.

get.summary: Read a recipe at its served version, or at `version`.

patch.summary: Send the whole recipe again as its next version. `expectedVersion` must be the latest version, or the answer is 412.

post.summary: Make a version the served one (the latest unless `version` names another). It must have passed its evaluation; activation signs it.

Check a version (the latest unless `version` names another) against the catalog and the data protection policy as they are now, and store the result on it. A version is served only after its last evaluation passed. On a plan with evaluations, when an eval set is attached to the recipe’s eval target (`model.targetId`), a model run follows: the version passes only after the run ends, when the recipe reaches the goal in at least 80% of the cases and at least 5 points more often than the same model without it. `model.status` is `pending` until then (follow the run, `model.runId`, in the evaluation API), and activating the version is refused until it has passed.
Copy a platform recipe into the organization as a draft. Once served, it replaces the platform recipe for this organization.

Make the served version of a recipe (or `version`) into a draft skill that belongs to the caller. The recipe version must verify against the published keys. The draft is private and cannot be installed until it passes the usual publish checks and review; the recipe’s eval cases are copied to the skill when the plan allows evaluations.

url.description: Path of the skill’s page on the gateway.

casesSkipped.description: Why no eval cases were copied, when the plan does not allow them. The draft was made.

post.summary: End a recipe for good. It is no longer served or changed and no longer counts against the plan.
Serve an earlier version again. It must have passed its evaluation.
Stop serving a recipe. It stays readable; activating a version serves it again.

get.summary: What changed between two versions of a recipe: `from` defaults to the served version and `to` to the latest. With `against=platform`, an organization recipe that overrides a platform recipe is compared with that platform recipe: the version it was copied from against the one served now.

from.description: The version compared from; with `against=platform`, the platform version the copy was made from.

to.description: The version compared to; with `against=platform`, the platform version served now.

get.summary: Read the stored evaluation verdict of a recipe version, the served one unless `version` is given: whether it passed, its score, the run that produced it and when. `state` is `running` while a model run is still going.

How often each version of a recipe was offered in a search (`served`) and read in full (`fetched`) by this organization over the last `days` days. Counts are the organization’s own, also for a platform recipe. `followed`, `succeeded` and `failed` come from the organization’s own recorded sessions, counted once a day, and stay 0 where mining of its usage is off.

followed.description: Recorded sessions whose required steps ran in the recipe’s order, whether or not the recipe was offered.

succeeded.description: Of the followed sessions, those whose last required step worked.

failed.description: Of the followed sessions, those whose last required step failed.

successRate.description: The 95% interval of the share that worked among followed sessions; null with none.

get.summary: List the versions of a recipe, oldest first, with the hash of each version’s content.

The public keys recipe signatures are checked against: only keys that are not revoked, public halves only. Needs no credential and may be cached for five minutes; fetch it again when a signature names an unknown key id.

publicKey.description: The raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, base64.

get.summary: Read a release and its site: its state while it is built, its warnings, and why it failed.

post.summary: Get an address that opens the release on its preview host already signed in, for showing the preview in a frame of the dashboard.

url.description: An address that signs the caller in on the release's preview host and opens it. It works once, within a minute.

get.summary: List the runs you started, newest first, or every run of the organization with scope=all (administrators). Skill evaluation runs are left out unless include=eval.

One run with its output, the governed calls it made and, for an agent run, its transcript. Another member's run is answered as not found, except to an administrator, who sees its metadata but not its output.

post.summary: Stop a run that is still going. Its token stops working at once and an agent loop notices before its next model or tool call.

Send a message to an agent run that is going. A steer message is read before the run's next model call; a follow_up is read when the run would otherwise finish, and the run goes on. Up to 20 messages of 4 KB per run. Only the person who started the run, or an administrator, may send one; agent credentials may not.

get.summary: The SCIM base URL of the organization and its tokens.

post.summary: Create a SCIM token. The token is in the answer once and cannot be read again. Confirmed with a passkey.

delete.summary: Revoke a SCIM token. The identity provider using it stops being able to provision at once.

get.summary: The fields and scopes needed to create an auth config for a service.
List the project’s saved session configs.

post.summary: Save a session policy under a name, to apply to many sessions by `configId`. It may only tighten the organization’s policy.

delete.summary: Delete a saved config. Sessions that used it keep the policy they have.

get.summary: Read a saved session config.

patch.summary: Rename a saved config or replace its policy; either starts a new version. Live sessions keep their policy unless `propagate` is true, which applies the new one to each and writes a history entry.

get.summary: List the project’s sessions, optionally one end user’s.

post.summary: Create a session for an end user: the policy their agent runs under. A policy can only tighten the organization’s.

delete.summary: Delete a session: its tokens stop working and it is gone.

get.summary: Read a session. A session token reads its own session only.

patch.summary: Change a session’s policy. Maps and policy blocks replace, the other blocks merge, null clears. A stale expectedConfigVersion is a 409 and changes nothing.

get.summary: Every version of a session’s policy, newest first.

post.summary: Report how an authorized custom call went, for the session’s log and the audit trail. Custom calls are not metered.
Ask whether the builder’s process may run one of the session’s custom tools with arguments of this digest. A write or destructive tool is held for a person; nothing is run by the gateway.

Run one tool in a session. A call that waits for an approval, a connection or a choice of account answers input_required with a requestState; send it back with the same tool and arguments to continue. The same Idempotency-Key returns the first outcome.

get.summary: List the files of the session, newest first. Only code running in this session reads or writes them, and they are deleted with it.

post.summary: Start an upload into the session’s folder: returns the address to send the bytes to, then complete the upload.

delete.summary: Delete one file of the session.

get.summary: A short-lived address to download one clean file of the session.

post.summary: Confirm the bytes arrived; the file is scanned before it can be downloaded or used by code.

get.summary: What happened in the session, newest first: tool calls, approvals and runs with their status, risk and duration. Never arguments or results.
List what the session remembers, by key.

delete.summary: Forget one key.

get.summary: Read one remembered value.

put.summary: Remember a JSON value of at most 16 KB under a key. A session keeps at most 256 keys; the memory is gone with the session.

get.summary: List a session’s tokens. Secrets are never returned.

post.summary: Mint a token for one session. It lasts at most 24 hours and is shown once; a dpopJkt binds it to a key.

delete.summary: Revoke a session token.

get.summary: The tools the session’s policy lets it run, named `<service>.<tool>` with their input schemas, for handing to a model API.
The organization’s switches for skills drafted from sessions.

put.summary: Change the organization’s switches, retention and the terms every capture redacts. The terms are never read back.

get.summary: List the sites the caller can open. The deleted ones, still restorable, are listed with status=deleted for their owners.

delete.summary: Delete a site. It stops serving at once and can be restored until the trash period of the plan ends.

get.summary: Read a site. Editors also get who it is shared with.

patch.summary: Change the title or routing of a site. Letting people download its source files is the owner’s decision.

post.summary: Ask the owner of a site for access. Asking twice while a request is open does not notify the owner again.
Make a ready release the live one, or go back to an earlier release. Who can open the site does not change.

get.summary: List the releases of a site, newest first. Editors only.

post.summary: Restore a deleted site. It comes back private, with only its owner able to open it.

put.summary: Show (mode=propose) or apply (mode=apply) the whole desired audience of a site. Applying needs the policy revision from the proposal; going public needs a passkey confirmation and a clean data protection scan.

post.summary: Start connecting a Slack workspace: returns the Slack address to send the admin to. Needs a passkey confirmation of the install.

delete.summary: Remove the single sign-on connection. Confirmed with a passkey.

get.summary: Read the organization's single sign-on connection.

put.summary: Create or change the single sign-on connection. Confirmed with a passkey.

get.summary: The most recent sign-in attempts through the connection, newest first.

post.summary: Start a test sign-in. Open the returned address in this browser; the connection can be turned on after one succeeds.
Start connecting a Microsoft 365 tenant: returns the Microsoft admin consent address to send the admin to. Needs a passkey confirmation of the connection.

get.summary: The events a connected service can send: each type’s config, the JSON Schema of its payload and a sample.
One trigger type.
List the project’s trigger instances. Each filter takes a comma-separated list; disabled instances are left out unless asked for.

post.summary: Create a trigger instance for one end user: a catalog trigger type fed by the account that user connected. Its events are delivered to the project’s subscriptions and stream.

delete.summary: Delete a trigger instance and remove its hook at the provider.

get.summary: Read a trigger instance.

patch.summary: Turn a trigger instance on or off, or rename it. Turning one on needs its provider hook to be in place.

post.summary: Try the provider again for an instance whose hook could not be made.
Declare the files of a release and get a signed upload slot for each file the organization does not already store.
Start building the release from the uploaded files. The release is polled until it is ready or failed.
Make the ingress endpoint of a custom OAuth app. Repeating the call for the same app returns the endpoint that exists.

get.summary: Read an ingress endpoint.

patch.summary: Change the setup fields named in the request. The address never changes.

put.summary: Set every setup field of the app’s endpoint. The address never changes.

get.summary: The fields an OAuth app of the project needs for its events, and its endpoint if one exists. Field values are written once and never returned.
List the project’s subscriptions.

post.summary: Subscribe an https address to the project’s events. The signing secret is shown once.

delete.summary: Delete a subscription.

get.summary: Read a subscription.

patch.summary: Change a subscription’s address, event types or description, or pause and resume it.

post.summary: Make a new signing secret, shown once. The old one keeps verifying for a day.

browserSession.description: A signed-in member session or member key.

workloadToken.description: A short-lived policy token a repository's CI job gets by trading its identity token at `/api/policy/ci/token`.
